selection_reasoning: These four tasks form a coherent multi-hop chain. First, the agent must mine sugar_cane (which is needed to craft paper). In parallel, the agent must mine kelp and build a pool (the pool provides the water environment where kelp grows, so building the pool is a prerequisite for mining kelp). Finally, selling paper requires having paper, which is crafted from sugar_cane. This creates a meaningful dependency structure: sugar_cane feeds into selling paper (via crafting), and building the pool enables kelp harvesting. The pool-building also adds a construction task that is observable and verifiable.

edges.reason: Kelp grows in water; the pool provides the water source where kelp is placed for mining
Paper is crafted from sugar_cane; agent needs sugar_cane inventory to craft paper before selling
Selling paper at the villager shop requires completing all gathering tasks first as a progression gate

milestones.description: Uses count_in_box_at_least (kind=block, object=water) to verify water blocks have been placed in the pool pit ABOVE the initial water layer. The pit is at spawn-relative [5,5] to [7,7] with initial water only at y=-3. Checking for water at y=-2 to y=-1 (above initial layer) confirms the player has filled the pool with buckets. This is a place/build task so count_in_box_at_least is the appropriate rule type. A generous box is used covering the full pit interior above the pre-existing water.

Uses inventory_has to check that the player has obtained kelp in their inventory. The player starts with 0 kelp, so having at least 1 confirms successful mining. Mining kelp underwater drops kelp items into inventory. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks since the mined drop ends up in inventory.

Uses inventory_has to check that the player has obtained sugar_cane in their inventory. The player starts with 0 sugar_cane (none given in inventory), so having at least 1 confirms successful mining from the planted sugar cane blocks. This is the preferred rule type for mine tasks since the mined drop ends up in inventory.

Uses inventory_has to check that the player has obtained at least 1 emerald. The player starts with 0 emeralds. The librarian villager's trade exchanges 3 paper for 1 emerald. Having an emerald in inventory confirms paper was successfully crafted from sugar_cane and sold to the villager. This is chosen because selling results in receiving emeralds in inventory.

scene_description: A flat grass area with three key elements: (1) A 3x3 stone-brick-bordered pool pit (3 blocks deep) at ~5-7, with water and kelp at the bottom — player must fill it with water using buckets to build the pool and then mine kelp; (2) Two sets of 3-tall sugar cane growing on sand adjacent to water at ~3,-3 and ~5,-3; (3) A librarian villager at ~-3,0,0 offering 1 emerald for 3 paper. Player has buckets, stone bricks, and a crafting table.
task_text: Build a pool by filling the stone brick pit with water, mine kelp from the pool, mine sugar cane, craft paper from sugar cane, and sell paper to the librarian villager for emeralds.
design_notes: Layout: Player spawns at origin on flat grass. Pool pit at SE (~5-7, ~5-7), sugar cane at E (~3,-3 and ~5,-3), villager at W (~-3,0). Pool is 3x3x3 deep with 1 water layer + kelp at bottom. Player must: (1) fill pool with water using buckets from sugar cane water sources, (2) mine kelp from pool, (3) mine 6 sugar cane, (4) craft paper on crafting table, (5) trade 3 paper to villager for emerald. No starting sugar_cane in inventory forces mining.
